annotations.text:
Nine full screens, one chrome, light only.

The first pass hand-copied the chrome and it drifted — some artboards had no nav at all and the response pane moved between them. These are generated from one template (build.mjs), so the top bar, rail, 288px tree, breadcrumb and pane padding are identical by construction, not by care.

Row 1 is the connector. Rows 2–3 are one action's tabs. The last is the founder's own API.

A connector has no tabs. Property table, Actions table, Agents strip — all on screen at once.

Auth is two rows of that table; screen 2 shows the credentials open, with the In column (Header / Query / Body) that makes an ?api_key= API configurable at all.

Screen 3 is a connector with nothing in it: no empty-state message, no Add button — the last row of the table is the affordance.

One tab row, ever, and it lives inside an action.

Response is pinned to the foot of the pane on EVERY action screen — a 44px "Not sent yet" strip until you Send, then 268px with the status line and the body. It does not move between tabs.

Every table is the same five columns: Key · Type · Source · Description · Required.

The founder's own API, mapped: 13 fields under one `detail` object.

day, month, year, lat and lon are required by the API and every one shows a dash — Meta records required-ness only for TOP-LEVEL body fields, and the only top-level field here is `detail`. So the description carries the range, the unit and the word required. There is no min, max or pattern either.

And the response: 200 OK with status:failed. A green tick on the status line would report success on a failed call, so the pane shows the body and the strip says read status, not the code.
